title: Twelve hundred Pearl bodies in the game, measured in a headed Chrome on the M4: a column marching down the lane holds the frame to the gate; a pile of them at the hull's feet is GPU-bound at 20-30 fps; the crowd cap sinks to 400 under it (owner, 2026-10-15: 'confirm that we can have up to 1200 enemies as in our dev lab tests')
context: Owner, 2026-10-15, unifying :8159 and :8162 on main 383006a6 (every serving worktree fast-forwarded to it): '3) confirm that we can have up to 1200 enemies as in our dev lab tests'. The lab's reading (2026-10-14-swarm-lab-pearl-mode, PEARL_WAVES's comment) was 1,200 bodies at ~58 fps in a 480 m file at the game's camera height, 60 draw calls. Headless frame times mean nothing, so three probes ran in a HEADED Chrome on this machine (scratch scripts crowd-view.mjs and crowd-lane.mjs beside the harness's --crowd-probe, the page index.html?sw=0&acceptance=1&cine=0&world=story&skip=defence&fps=1#td, the Pearl default, sectorQuiet, spawnFodder 70% amoeba / 20% ghost / 10% phage, the chase view). The window's frame sat at exactly 20.0 ms at rest in every run (the compositor's cadence here), so 20 ms is the floor, not a cost.
outcome: (1) The crowd out of view (the harness's --crowd-probe, the camera at the base): 300 to 1,500 alive, frame 20.0 ms throughout, the enemies' CPU 0.4 -> 2.1 ms, draw calls flat (~1,700: the bodies are instanced a tier a call), gpu 13-15 ms. The step is not the cost. (2) The column (crowd-lane.mjs): 1,279 alive rising at the far breach and marching on the gate, the tank parked at the Rotor's socket: at 1440x900 the frame held 20.0 ms from 25 cells out to 4 cells out (gpu 14-18 ms, triangles 1.4M -> 2.4M as the hulls grew), gpu 22 ms at 2 cells, 35 ms with the head of the column at the hull (frame 24 ms, 41 fps, the end screenshot). At 3440x1353 (the owner's ultrawide): 20.0 ms to 8 cells out (gpu 17-20), gpu 25 at 6 cells, 30 at 3, 32 at 1 cell (frame 22-26 ms). (3) The pile (crowd-view.mjs): bodies up at one cell with the tank parked in them: 600 alive, frame 27.5 ms, gpu 30 (the gunship's thermal zoom over them 33 ms); 1,500 alive (1,050 around the hull, RAM x456 at once), frame 48.6 ms, gpu 57 ms, 7.3M triangles, 511 calls, the enemies' CPU 6 ms. Read: the game holds twelve hundred Pearl bodies as a crowd on the lane, which is what a wave is; what it does not hold at 60 fps is hundreds of them filling the frame at arm's length (the membrane's transparent fill over the whole screen, many layers deep, plus the near hulls: fill-bound, not count-bound, so the ultrawide pays ~2x there). Under that pile the crowd cap (CROWD_CAP slowMs 36) came down from 1,500 to 400 in the 600-body run and stayed there, which holds every later wave in the queue: the owner's 'waves are smaller' has this in it as well as PEARL_WAVES. Not measured: a real sector's mixed tiers (cores, squads) at this count; the frame with bloom or the membrane's passes switched off (no URL flag for either); 100 Hz output (the probe window ran at 50).
alternatives: Take the lab's 58 fps as the game's: rejected, the lab draws 60 calls over a file of small bodies; the game's cost is the near pile.
Measure headless with --crowd-probe: rejected, headless frame times mean nothing (2026-10-13-pearl-enemies-story-mode).
A count cap for the owner's 1,200: the reading says the cap wants to be on screen fill (near bodies, pixels), not on count; left as the next move for the rework of the waves.
evidence: HEADED=1 STALHEART_BROWSER_PORT=18171 COUNTS=300,600,900,1200,1200,1200,1500,1500,1500 node scripts/browser-test.mjs --crowd-probe (scratch log crowd-headed.log): frame 20.0 ms at every count, cpu enemies 0.4 -> 2.1 ms, calls 1,595-1,707, gpu 10.7-15.3 ms
